attributes.name: Earth
attributes.description: Raw physical power and endurance - how strong you are, how hard you hit, how much punishment your body shrugs off.

attributes.name: Air
attributes.description: Agility, adaptability, and sharpness of mind - how fast you react, how well you keep pace with a changing situation, how clearly you think under pressure.

attributes.name: Fire
attributes.description: Drive and aggression - how hard you push, how much force of will and personality you bring to a confrontation, verbal or physical.

attributes.name: Water
attributes.description: Perception and empathy - how attuned you are to the world and the people in it, and how much you can endure before you're worn down.

attributes.name: Moira
attributes.description: Fate, destiny, and the supernatural - the part of you touched by forces bigger than the mundane world, governing luck, combat instinct, and your connection to whatever is otherworldly about you.

subStats.name: Soak
subStats.description: Resists Physical damage - the wall an attacker's dice have to beat to hurt you.

subStats.name: Potence
subStats.description: Raw strength - carrying capacity, forcing/breaking things, contested strength.

subStats.name: Psyche
subStats.description: Resists Mental attacks, and sets how many dice you roll when making one.

subStats.name: Ferocity
subStats.description: Boosts a Physical attack die when you spend Ki to push a strike.

subStats.name: Presence
subStats.description: Resists Social attacks, and sets how many dice you roll when making one.

subStats.name: Stamina
subStats.description: Caps how many Fate Tokens you can hold (× 3) and how many you can spend per Scene; also your endurance against non-combat exhaustion.

subStats.name: Health
subStats.description: Feeds your Health Levels (how many hits you can take).

subStats.name: Atropos
subStats.description: Feeds Defense (how hard you are to touch at all - blade, word, or mind).

subStats.name: Klotho
subStats.description: Ki Regeneration rate and your Lucky Number.

natures.name: Analyst
natures.drive: You read the manual. All of it, including the safety pages, for the thing everybody else already plugged in and started using. You have been right about this often enough that it has stopped being funny.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you stop everyone to work out how the thing actually works, and the delay costs you the opening you had

natures.name: Avenger
natures.drive: You remember the name. It has been years and you could still spell it, still pick the face out of a crowd, still say exactly what was done and in what order.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you go after the person who earned it instead of the thing that would have helped, and it makes everything harder

natures.name: Caregiver
natures.drive: You carry plasters. Actual plasters, in your actual bag, along with paracetamol and a spare charger and a bottle of water that is not for you. Somebody always needs one and you have stopped pretending to be surprised.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you stop to look after somebody while the clock is running, and it costs you the window

natures.name: Charmer
natures.drive: You have been let into places you had no business being, by people who could not explain afterwards why they opened the door. Nobody has ever described you as pushy.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you turn somebody hostile into somebody helpful on nothing but conversation, somewhere force would have been quicker

natures.name: Competitor
natures.drive: You have turned a walk to the shop into a race. Against yourself. And won, and felt good about it, and told nobody.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you push past what the job actually needed because somebody was keeping score, or might have been

natures.name: Daredevil
natures.drive: There is a video of you. Several people have asked you to take it down. You have watched it more times than any of them.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you take the option with the drop, the speed or the odds, and the safe one was sitting right there

natures.name: Diplomat
natures.drive: Two people who cannot stand each other have both told you their side. Neither of them knows you spoke to the other one. You are still holding both.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you talk two sides down instead of picking one, and picking one would have been faster

natures.name: Enforcer
natures.drive: You keep a note of what people owe. Not on your phone. On paper, somewhere, in handwriting that is not quite your normal handwriting.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you make somebody answer for a broken word, at a moment when letting it go would have cost you nothing

natures.name: Fixer
natures.drive: You know a guy. You knew a guy before anybody had finished saying what the problem was. Your phone is mostly numbers with no names attached to them.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you solve it with a favour, a name or an angle, in a room where everybody else had already reached for something heavier

natures.name: Ghost
natures.drive: You have never been tagged in a photograph. You have checked. You check about once a month and you do not think that is strange.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you choose to go unseen or unrecorded, and being known would have got it done quicker

natures.name: Guardian
natures.drive: You sit facing the door. You found the exits before you sat down, and you already know which of the people at this table would not make it to one.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you hold your ground over something you have claimed, and moving would have been the sensible thing to do

natures.name: Idealist
natures.drive: You still sign the petitions. You know the numbers. You have read the same article about how little it changes, twice, and you signed one this morning.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you take the principled option out loud, in front of people who had already reached for the cynical one

natures.name: Judge
natures.drive: You have ended a dinner party. You were right, which did not help, and you would say it again, which is the part people find difficult.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you name what somebody did, to their face, when saying nothing would have cost you nothing

natures.name: Leader
natures.drive: When it goes quiet and everybody looks at each other, they end up looking at you. You have never worked out when that started.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you make the call nobody wanted to make, and then stand in front of what it costs

natures.name: Loner
natures.drive: You have moved a sofa up a flight of stairs by yourself. It took four hours. Three people would have come if you had called, and you did not call.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you turn down help or peel off from the group, and doing it together would obviously have worked better

natures.name: Mentor
natures.drive: Somebody still has your old notes. You copied them out neater before you handed them over, and you have never mentioned that to anyone.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you stand back so somebody else takes the lesson, the lead or the credit, on a job you could have done faster yourself

natures.name: Opportunist
natures.drive: You have made money out of a very bad week that was happening to somebody else. You did not cause it. You would like that on the record.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you turn somebody's disaster into your own advantage while it is still going on

natures.name: Perfectionist
natures.drive: You have rewritten a text message four times before sending it. It was three sentences long. You are aware of how that sounds and it did not change anything.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you refuse to hand over a result everybody else had already accepted, and the delay hurts

natures.name: Protector
natures.drive: You walk on the traffic side. You do it without noticing, you do it for everybody, and you have done it for people you do not like.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you take the hit, the risk or the loss that was coming for somebody who could not have taken it

natures.name: Rebel
natures.drive: You have read a sign, understood it completely, and done the other thing. Not for a reason. The sign was the reason.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you break a rule specifically because somebody with authority gave it, and following it would have been easier

natures.name: Showman
natures.drive: You have an entrance. You have practised it. You have a second one for when the first would be too much, and you have used that one considerably less.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you make it a performance, at the cost of your cover, your subtlety, or a perfectly good plan

natures.name: Skeptic
natures.drive: You have looked something up in front of the person who told you. They did not enjoy it. You have done it again since, to somebody else.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you refuse the easy explanation and go and look, while everybody else is relieved and moving on

natures.name: Survivor
natures.drive: You have eaten worse and slept somewhere worse, and you would do both again tomorrow without making a thing of it.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you take the ugly, practical option in front of people who would much rather you took the proud one

natures.name: Trickster
natures.drive: You have got into a building with a clipboard and a confident walk. Nobody stopped you. Somebody held a door.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you get it done with a lie, a misdirection or a bit, when walking in and asking would have worked

natures.name: True Believer
natures.drive: There is one thing you will not do. Everybody who knows you knows what it is, and two of them have tested it.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you keep to the code at the exact moment breaking it would have solved everything

natures.name: Wanderer
natures.drive: Everything you own fits in the car. You have checked recently, which probably tells you something about where your head is.
natures.example: Take a Fate Token when you walk away from a place, a group or a claim that had started to look permanent

skillTiers.name: Expert
skillTiers.roll: Attribute + Difficulty, with Advantage, and **critical success widens to a roll of 2 or 3**

skillTiers.name: Master
skillTiers.roll: Same as Expert, plus: **on a catastrophic failure, roll again** - if the second roll succeeds, it's treated as a normal failure, not a catastrophic failure

skillCatalog.name: Academics
skillCatalog.definition: General scholarship, history, and literature.

skillCatalog.name: Acrobatics
skillCatalog.definition: Balance, tumbling, and controlled falls.

skillCatalog.name: Animal Handling
skillCatalog.definition: Training, calming, and directing animals.

skillCatalog.name: Appraisal
skillCatalog.definition: Judging the value and authenticity of goods.

skillCatalog.name: Archery
skillCatalog.definition: Which bows you are trained on, by Category: hand crossbow, then crossbow, recurve, compound, and the warbow at Master. Never rolled for an attack - see [Weapon Skills Are Not Attack Skills](#weapon-skills-are-not-attack-skills).

skillCatalog.name: Athletics
skillCatalog.definition: Running, jumping, climbing, and lifting under exertion.

skillCatalog.name: Barter
skillCatalog.definition: Striking favorable trades and deals.

skillCatalog.name: Bribery
skillCatalog.definition: Knowing how much, how, and who to pay to get what you want.

skillCatalog.name: Bureaucracy
skillCatalog.definition: Navigating institutions, paperwork, permits, and red tape to get things done.

skillCatalog.name: Charm
skillCatalog.definition: Ingratiation and drawing people in.

skillCatalog.name: Combat Driving/Piloting
skillCatalog.definition: Operating a vehicle under fire or in a chase. This is a separate Skill from ordinary Driving or Piloting; competence in traffic says nothing about competence under fire.

skillCatalog.name: Composition
skillCatalog.definition: Writing music, poetry, or stories with real craft.

skillCatalog.name: Computer Use
skillCatalog.definition: General computing, software, and programming. This Skill is distinct from Hacking - the same machine, but one of you is asking it politely.

skillCatalog.name: Concealment
skillCatalog.definition: Hiding objects, caches, or hideouts from a determined search.

skillCatalog.name: Contortion
skillCatalog.definition: Fitting through tight spaces and slipping restraints through flexibility.

skillCatalog.name: Cooking
skillCatalog.definition: Preparing food, from the everyday to the exceptional.

skillCatalog.name: Covert Signals
skillCatalog.definition: Prearranged signals that carry meaning without words - hand signs, chalk marks, whistles, and brevity over the air.

skillCatalog.name: Crafting
skillCatalog.definition: Building and repairing goods in a chosen trade. One Skill covers any material or trade - woodworking, metalworking, whatever you practice - because the habits of hand and eye carry across all of them.

skillCatalog.name: Cryptography
skillCatalog.definition: Creating and breaking codes, ciphers, and encryption.

skillCatalog.name: Deception
skillCatalog.definition: Lying, bluffing, and fast talk.

skillCatalog.name: Demolitions
skillCatalog.definition: Safely handling, placing, and detonating explosives.

skillCatalog.name: Disguise
skillCatalog.definition: Altering appearance and behaviors to convincingly pass as someone else.

skillCatalog.name: Divination
skillCatalog.definition: Reading omens, portents, and the shape of what’s coming.

skillCatalog.name: Driving
skillCatalog.definition: Operating ground vehicles in ordinary traffic and terrain.

skillCatalog.name: Electronics
skillCatalog.definition: Building, repairing, and modifying electronic devices and circuitry.

skillCatalog.name: Engineering
skillCatalog.definition: Theoretical and design knowledge of structures and systems.

skillCatalog.name: Escapology
skillCatalog.definition: Breaking free of restraints and confined spaces under pressure.

skillCatalog.name: Etiquette
skillCatalog.definition: Navigating social and professional protocol correctly.

skillCatalog.name: Farming
skillCatalog.definition: Cultivating crops and managing livestock.

skillCatalog.name: Finance
skillCatalog.definition: Economics, markets, and accounting.

skillCatalog.name: Firearms
skillCatalog.definition: Which firearms you are trained on, by Category: handgun, then shotgun, submachine gun, rifle, and the heavy weapons at Master. Never rolled for an attack - see [Weapon Skills Are Not Attack Skills](#weapon-skills-are-not-attack-skills).

skillCatalog.name: First Aid
skillCatalog.definition: Immediate, field-level treatment - stabilizing, bandaging, CPR.

skillCatalog.name: Fishing
skillCatalog.definition: Catching fish by line, net, or spear.

skillCatalog.name: Forgery
skillCatalog.definition: Producing convincing fake documents, signatures, IDs, and digital records.

skillCatalog.name: Gaming
skillCatalog.definition: Skill at games of strategy, chance, and wagering - tabletop, esports, or otherwise.

skillCatalog.name: Hacking
skillCatalog.definition: Bypassing digital security - accounts, networks, cameras, and devices.

skillCatalog.name: Holistic Medicine
skillCatalog.definition: Herbal remedies, folk medicine, and non-clinical healing traditions.

skillCatalog.name: Hunting
skillCatalog.definition: Tracking, catching, and field-dressing game.

skillCatalog.name: Insight
skillCatalog.definition: Reading people, sensing motive and deception - a read that goes past ordinary attention.

skillCatalog.name: Interrogation
skillCatalog.definition: Extracting information from an unwilling subject.

skillCatalog.name: Intimidation
skillCatalog.definition: Coercing others through implied or explicit threat.

skillCatalog.name: Intrigue
skillCatalog.definition: Scheming, maneuvering, and reading the undercurrents of institutional or political conflict.

skillCatalog.name: Invention
skillCatalog.definition: Designing and building original devices, not just following existing plans.

skillCatalog.name: Investigation
skillCatalog.definition: Following clues at a scene and drawing sound conclusions.

skillCatalog.name: Law
skillCatalog.definition: Legal codes, procedure, and precedent.

skillCatalog.name: Leadership
skillCatalog.definition: Commanding respect and rallying others to act.

skillCatalog.name: Linguistics
skillCatalog.definition: Learning, translating, and analyzing languages.

skillCatalog.name: Mechanics
skillCatalog.definition: Repair and maintenance of vehicles and machinery.

skillCatalog.name: Medicine
skillCatalog.definition: Surgery, diagnosis, and long-term clinical treatment.

skillCatalog.name: Melee Weapons
skillCatalog.definition: Which melee weapons you are trained on, by Category: improvised and knives, then one-handed blunt and large blades, one-handed blades, polearms and two-handers, and the exotic ones at Master. Never rolled for an attack - see [Weapon Skills Are Not Attack Skills](#weapon-skills-are-not-attack-skills).

skillCatalog.name: Navigation
skillCatalog.definition: Plotting a course and avoiding getting lost, on foot, by vehicle, or otherwise.

skillCatalog.name: Networking
skillCatalog.definition: Building and leveraging connections in professional, corporate, or elite circles.

skillCatalog.name: Occult
skillCatalog.definition: Esoteric lore, ritual, and the world’s hidden supernatural undercurrent.

skillCatalog.name: Perception
skillCatalog.definition: Noticing details and spotting hidden things.

skillCatalog.name: Performance
skillCatalog.definition: Acting, music, dance, or oratory before an audience, under one Skill whatever the medium.

skillCatalog.name: Persuasion
skillCatalog.definition: Honest argument and diplomacy.

skillCatalog.name: Piloting
skillCatalog.definition: Operating aircraft or watercraft, under one Skill whatever the vehicle.

skillCatalog.name: Politics
skillCatalog.definition: The workings of governments, agencies, and factions.

skillCatalog.name: Psychology
skillCatalog.definition: Understanding minds, motivations and behavior, including therapy and the long-term treatment of mental trauma.

skillCatalog.name: Public Speaking
skillCatalog.definition: Commanding a room and structuring a spoken argument. This is a separate Skill from Performance - one is argument, the other is spectacle, and being good at one promises nothing about the other.

skillCatalog.name: Religion
skillCatalog.definition: Theology, doctrine, and religious practice.

skillCatalog.name: Research
skillCatalog.definition: Finding information through records, libraries, databases, and open sources. This is a separate Skill from Investigation: Investigation reads a scene, Research reads the record.

skillCatalog.name: Ridicule
skillCatalog.definition: Mockery, insult, and the cutting remark. Roasting, trash talk, and the dozens. Distinct from Intimidation, which threatens, and from Performance, which plays to a room rather than at somebody standing in it.

skillCatalog.name: Science
skillCatalog.definition: Broad scientific knowledge. One Skill covers every discipline - chemistry, biology, astrophysics - because a point spent here should buy you a scientist, not a specialist in one footnote.

skillCatalog.name: Security
skillCatalog.definition: Bypassing physical locks, safes, and alarm systems.

skillCatalog.name: Seduction
skillCatalog.definition: Winning someone over through romantic or physical appeal.

skillCatalog.name: Shadowing
skillCatalog.definition: Following someone without being noticed.

skillCatalog.name: Sleight of Hand
skillCatalog.definition: Pickpocketing, palming, and planting objects unnoticed.

skillCatalog.name: Smuggling
skillCatalog.definition: Concealing and moving contraband past scrutiny, including modern screening and customs.

skillCatalog.name: Stealth
skillCatalog.definition: Moving unseen and unheard.

skillCatalog.name: Streetwise
skillCatalog.definition: Navigating criminal culture, gangs, and underworld contacts.

skillCatalog.name: Surveillance
skillCatalog.definition: Observing a target or location without being detected, and spotting when somebody is doing it to you - physical stakeouts and technical monitoring both.

skillCatalog.name: Survival
skillCatalog.definition: Foraging, shelter, water, and enduring somewhere that offers no help.

skillCatalog.name: Swimming
skillCatalog.definition: Moving efficiently and enduring in open water. **Can't be used untrained:** without it you can't swim - see [Swimming](movement.md#swimming).

skillCatalog.name: Systems Operation
skillCatalog.definition: Operating and interpreting complex consoles, sensors, and industrial or vehicle control systems.

skillCatalog.name: Thrown Weapons
skillCatalog.definition: Which thrown weapons you are trained on, by Category: balanced blade, then thrown axe, shafted, returning, and the sling at Master. Never rolled for an attack - see [Weapon Skills Are Not Attack Skills](#weapon-skills-are-not-attack-skills).

skillCatalog.name: Tracking
skillCatalog.definition: Following physical trails.

boons.name: Alertness
boons.effect: Immune to being [Surprised](rules.md#surprised) while conscious, unless under a mind-altering effect that would specifically allow it.
boons.flavour: You are never *not* paying attention. While everyone else is asking, "What was that?" You are already turning to face the threat. You pay attention to everything... to the point of being called "paranoid" more than once.

boons.name: Alternate Identity
boons.effect: A fully realized second identity - name, history, and papers that hold up under real scrutiny - keeping your real self insulated from what it does.
boons.flavour: You have a second life. There's an address that receives your mail. There are neighbors who could describe you to a sketch artist without a second thought. It all stands up to scrutiny because it is all real. It's a lot of work, but worth it for the benefits it grants.

boons.name: Always Connected
boons.effect:
Bought as one of three tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one).
**Tier 1 (3, Lesser)**: your mobile/portable computing devices are always online under normal conditions - no dead zones, no dropped signal, no service gaps. Supernatural interference, deliberate technological jamming, or genuinely extreme circumstances (miles underground, fully off-grid) can still block it, GM's call, but ordinary everyday conditions never do.
**Tier 2 (5, Greater)**: the same connection, but it's not tied to any device - a cybernetic implant of your own, granting the same access even fully divested of every belonging and piece of gear you own.
**Tier 3 (7, Legendary)**: the same connection as Tier 2, but through some means beyond ordinary technology (a lingering enchantment, a telepathic relay, quantum entanglement, whatever fits the character) - unbreakable so long as you remain on this plane of existence, immune even to the exceptions Tier 1 allowed.
boons.flavour: You are the one who never says, "I don't have any bars!" There is always a signal and you are connected to it. While the rest of them are wandering around with their phones in the air, you've already sent the file.

boons.name: Ambidextrous
boons.effect:
Bought as one of three tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one).
**Tier 1 (3, Lesser)**: ignore the [Disadvantage](rules.md#advantage--disadvantage) normally imposed for performing a task with your off-hand.
**Tier 2 (5, Greater)**: your hands work independently - perform one task with each hand in the same round, instead of one task overall.
**Tier 3 (7, Legendary)**: once per turn, spend **1 Ki** to make one additional attack with your off-hand, at no penalty.
boons.flavour: Most people have a dominant hand. For you, whichever hand is free is the dominant one.

boons.name: Animal Rapport
boons.effect: Animals read you as safe and trustworthy on sight, calmer and friendlier around you than they'd otherwise be - no communication, just instinct.
boons.flavour: Dogs cross the street to greet you. The cat that no one gets to pet sits in your lap. Your friends describe you as a "Disney Princess," and they aren't wrong. You can't communicate with them and you can't tell them what to do. Animals just trust you on sight.

boons.name: Common Sense
boons.effect: The GM will give you a heads-up before you commit to an obviously terrible decision.
boons.flavour: Most people don't realize they did something stupid until it's too late. The little voice in the back of your head says, "I wouldn't do that. It's a bad idea." And you listen. Most of the time. When you do something stupid, you can't say nobody warned you.

boons.name: Compact Frame
boons.effect: Fit through spaces, gaps, and crowds an ordinary body couldn't, and blend into a packed room without trying.
boons.flavour: When other people have to squeeze into a tight space, you just walk on through. Vents, the space behind the cabinet, the crowd other people have to muscle their way through are non-issues for you. It works the other way, too - you can easily disappear in a crowd.

boons.name: Concentration
boons.effect: Immune to being [Distracted](rules.md#distracted), regardless of source (damage, Kotodama, Gifts, environmental hazards) - a Slow action always resolves as declared.
boons.flavour: Once you start something, you will finish it. You studied for finals in a bar during a GWAR concert and aced them. Gunfire, explosions, a demolition crew tearing the building down around you - none of it is a distraction.

boons.name: Danger Sense
boons.effect: May ask the GM at any reasonable moment whether there's danger nearby; the GM must give a truthful (if vague, gut-feeling-level) answer. Additionally, roll **2d10 for Initiative and keep the higher die** (instead of the normal single 1d10), then add your Initiative sub-stat as usual.
boons.flavour: It's quiet... Too quiet. Something is wrong. You don't know what it is, you just know. Something warns you when you are in danger.

boons.name: Displaced Echoes
boons.effect:
Bought as one of two tiers (the higher includes the lower's benefit - no need to buy both).
**Tier 1 (3, Lesser)**: perfectly imitate any voice or sound you've heard - undetectable unless a listener has a specific reason to doubt it, in which case they may roll Insight + Difficulty (GM sets Difficulty by how good their reason for suspicion is) to see through it.
**Tier 2 (5, Greater)**: additionally, throw your voice to make it seem to originate from any point in your line of sight.
boons.flavour: Mockingbirds, magpies and you. You hear a car alarm, a chainsaw, a snippet of a song and can imitate it perfectly. It's not an impression, but you mimic the sound precisely.

boons.name: Distinctive Features
boons.effect:
Bought as one of four tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one). None are purely cosmetic - they have real effects.
Choose a feature: **Tail** (real balance and grip - another hand for holding on, not for fine work), **Gills** (breathe water indefinitely, and air as normal), **Fur** (ignore cold that has everybody else reaching for a coat), **Pouch** (a few small items carried hands-free and out of sight), or **Coloration** (markings nobody would mistake for human, and blending into one matching environment you name). Anything else that size works too, if you and the GM can agree what it does.
**Tier 1 (1, Trivial)**: one feature.
**Tier 2 (3, Lesser)**: a second.
**Tier 3 (5, Greater)**: a third.
**Tier 4 (7, Legendary)**: a fourth.
boons.flavour: There is something about you that is visibly different. You might have something non-human in the family tree or you might have Bette Davis eyes. Or a tail that helps you balance, gills, fur, markings that can't be mistaken for a birthmark. They are unusual, but useful.

boons.name: Double-Jointed
boons.effect: For Escapology rolls, treat your [Skill Training Tier](skills.md#training-tiers) as one tier higher than your actual tier, with a minimum of Trained - even an Untrained or Novice character rolls Escapology as if Trained. Trained rolls as if Adept, Adept as if Expert, Expert as if Master. (Master stays Master.)
boons.flavour: You saw a man fold himself into an acrylic box on The Gong Show and decided you wanted to do the same thing. Now, if you can get your head through it, the rest of you will follow.

boons.name: Duelist
boons.effect:
Bought as one of three tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one). Attacks are a straight Attribute-vs-Defense roll with no Skill involved, so no [Training Tier](skills.md#training-tiers) ever reaches them; this is that ladder, bought rather than trained.
**Tier 1 (3, Lesser)**: name one weapon Category from the [weapon Skills](skills.md#the-skill-list) - Knife, Handgun, Large blade, whatever you actually carry. Attack rolls made with it are at **[Advantage](rules.md#advantage--disadvantage)** - the same shape as **Adept**.
**Tier 2 (5, Greater)**: with that weapon, a **critical hit lands on a 2 or a 3** - the same shape as **Expert**.
**Tier 3 (7, Legendary)**: name a second Category, which gains both benefits. Held alongside [Never Off Balance](#boon-list), which supplies the **Master** tier, this completes the ladder for attacks.
boons.flavour: You picked a weapon and learned everything about it. It is no longer a tool - it is a part of you. The guy across from you has trained. You have specialized.

boons.name: Eidetic Memory
boons.effect:
Bought as one of two tiers (the higher includes the lower's benefit - no need to buy both).
**Tier 1 (5, Greater)**: perfect recall of anything you've actually experienced and attended to - things you saw, read, or heard.
**Tier 2 (7, Legendary)**: perfect recall of literally anything you've ever perceived, attended to or not - a page glimpsed once, background chatter, something in peripheral vision.
boons.flavour: Everyone else's memories fade and slowly rearrange themselves as time passes. Yours do not. You don't remember things, you access the files. The page is there in front of you. The license plate is on the car at the stoplight in your mind.

boons.name: Enchanting Voice
boons.effect: Anyone who hears you speak has their initial reaction/disposition nudged a step more favorably. Additionally, choose one voice-dependent Skill (Charm, Deception, Performance, Persuasion, Public Speaking, or Seduction) at creation: treat your [Skill Training Tier](skills.md#training-tiers) as one tier higher than your actual tier for that Skill, with a minimum of Trained (same shape as [Double-Jointed](#boon-list)'s Escapology bump).
boons.flavour: You could read the phone book and people would lean in to listen. The velvet tones of your voice rival the Sirens or Orpheus. Something in your voice makes people decide you are worth listening to. You can't switch it off.

boons.name: Encyclopedic Knowledge
boons.effect: When you want to know something relevant about a topic - history, science, esoteric trivia, nearly anything - roll **Air + Difficulty** directly (GM sets Difficulty by how obscure the fact is; no Skill or Training Tier involved). Success - the GM tells you the relevant fact, though you can't say where or how you learned it. Failure - nothing surfaces.
boons.flavour: You read something about this once. It was in a psychology journal. "Why did I read it? It seemed interesting." You devour information and it sticks with you. It doesn't matter where the information came from, you are almost always right.

boons.name: Extra Limbs
boons.effect:
Bought as one of four tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one). You have more limbs than an ordinary person - extra arms, tentacles, or something else the body has simply grown in, each one just as functional as your original set.
**Tier 1 (1, Trivial)**: one extra limb, usable for simple parallel tasks (hold, brace, steady something) alongside whatever you're already doing.
**Tier 2 (3, Lesser)**: two extra limbs - you can hold or ready an additional item at all times (a second weapon, a shield, a tool), always available without needing to draw it.
**Tier 3 (5, Greater)**: three extra limbs - they can actively assist a task you're already attempting, granting Advantage on any roll where an extra hand or two would help (Escapology, forcing/breaking something, climbing).
**Tier 4 (7, Legendary)**: four or more extra limbs, full independent use - perform up to two simple parallel tasks per round instead of one, and gain Advantage on any physical task benefiting from more hands, including grappling or restraining an opponent.
boons.flavour: Most humans have two arms and two legs. Some have less, which brings the average down. You are trying to bring the average back up. You have more limbs than a "normal" human. Whether it is more arms, legs, tentacles, they are yours. They work and your body has never been confused about their function. Complex tasks are easier, but finding a suit that fits is hard.

boons.name: Eye for the Opening
boons.effect: Your critical range on attack rolls widens - a roll of **2 or 3** is a [critical hit](rules.md#critical-hits), not just a 2. An attack uses no Skill, so no [Training Tier](skills.md#training-tiers) can widen it for you; this is the only thing that does. Applies to Physical, Social and Mental attacks alike.
boons.flavour: You don't hit harder than anyone else. You don't have to. You see the opportunity - when their guard dips, they are shifting their weight and are vulnerable or when their attention flickers to something behind you - and you seize that moment.

boons.name: Eye for the Strange
boons.effect: When something supernatural is happening around you, roll **Moira + Difficulty** directly (GM sets Difficulty by how subtle/hidden it is; no Skill or Training Tier involved). Success - the GM tells you something supernatural is present and gives you a relevant detail. Failure - you still feel something resonating in the threads of fate, leaving you uneasy with no concrete information.
boons.flavour: No one noticed, but when you walk into the room, you feel it. Something isn't natural and you can spot it - the shadows are too deep, there is a cold spot following a conversation. You can sense the supernatural.

boons.name: Familiar
boons.effect:
Bought as one of four tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one). Not necessarily magical, not necessarily built by you, just yours.
Choose what it is. What it is decides which Skills it can take:
**Bound spirit** - something that was never quite alive, tied to you by an arrangement neither of you brings up. It goes where you can't and notices what you wouldn't. *Divination, Insight, Occult, Perception, Religion, Shadowing, Surveillance.*
**Animated servant** - a made thing that runs on something and keeps running whether or not anybody is watching. Tireless, literal, and stronger than it looks. *Athletics, Crafting, Electronics, Mechanics, Security, Systems Operation.*
**Talking object** - a book, a ring, a radio that picks up more than it should. It doesn't move on its own, so it gets carried, and it is usually the best-read thing in the room. *Academics, Appraisal, Cryptography, Law, Linguistics, Occult, Research, Science.*
**Capable person** - somebody who works for you, follows you, or has decided you need looking after. *Any Skill a person could learn.*
**Tier 1 (1, Trivial)**: Trained in one Skill from its list. Reliably useful for everyday work, not built for danger.
**Tier 2 (3, Lesser)**: Expert in that Skill, plus Trained in two more from its list. Can act for you unsupervised on simple tasks.
**Tier 3 (5, Greater)**: Master in its specialty, and able to hold its own when things turn dangerous - a butler who is also a bodyguard, luggage that can flatten an attacker, a spirit with real teeth.
**Tier 4 (7, Legendary)**: a legend in its own right, recognised or feared independently of you. Effectively unkillable in any permanent sense - destroyed, it finds its way back, rebuilt, reformed or returned.
boons.flavour: You have someone... or something that has chosen you. A black cat followed you home. A book started talking to you one day. A spirit attached itself to you and never explained why. Whatever it is, it is competent, loyal and willing to go places you can't.

boons.name: Feign Death
boons.effect:
Bought as one of two tiers (the higher includes the lower's benefit - no need to buy both).
**Tier 1 (3, Lesser)**: convincingly fool onlookers - and a casual medical check - into believing you're dead or unconscious, on your own choice.
**Tier 2 (5, Greater)**: dead to all means of detection, including rigorous or technological examination - full voluntary control over your own vital signs and biofeedback, deep enough to fool sophisticated medical equipment.
boons.flavour: Your body is a biological machine and you have learned to shut the whole machine down... temporarily. You appear dead in every way that matters.

boons.name: Higher Purpose
boons.effect: Once per major story arc, you cannot be permanently killed or written out of the story by anything short of a dramatically appropriate death - you're meant for something greater, and the universe isn't done with you yet.
boons.flavour: You have been chosen for a specific purpose. By what? You don't know. It might be fate, a debt, an elder god. Whatever it is - it has a vested interest in seeing that your story ends after you achieve this goal. When you go, it will mean something.

boons.name: Innate Compass
boons.effect:
Bought as one of two tiers (the higher includes the lower's benefit - no need to buy both).
**Tier 1 (1, Trivial)**: always know true north and roughly what time it is, no matter where you are.
**Tier 2 (3, Lesser)**: additionally, for any place you've been before, you always know the direction and rough distance to it.
boons.flavour: You don't get lost. Ever. North is that way. It's just a fact you have access to, the same way you know which way is up. You always know roughly where you are, even without a map. That doesn't stop people from handing you the map, though.

boons.name: Iron Grip
boons.effect: Immune to being disarmed against your will - a weapon or item stays in your hand until you choose to let go.
boons.flavour: Your hand is a vise. If you have a grip on it - it stays in your hand.

boons.name: Iron Stomach
boons.effect: Eat or drink almost anything without illness.
boons.flavour: Gas station sushi. The leftovers with no clear date on them. Water out of something that isn't a tap. Whatever it is, you imbibe it, and then you are fine. Anyone who shared it with you - not so much.

boons.name: Iron Will
boons.effect:
Bought as one of three tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one).
**Tier 1 (3, Lesser)**: immune to being read via [Insight](skills.md#the-skill-list) - an attempt to read your emotions, tells, or intentions through Insight automatically fails.
**Tier 2 (5, Greater)**: additionally, any attempt to read or rewrite your mind - by Skill, Gift or anything else - is made at [Disadvantage](rules.md#advantage--disadvantage), and unlocks **Assert Your Will** as a [Fate Trigger](fate.md#fate-triggers) - spend 1 Fate Token to flatly negate an attempt to intimidate or dominate you, no roll.
**Tier 3 (7, Legendary)**: additionally, full passive immunity to domination, possession, mind control, memory alteration, and any attempt to read you whatsoever - no roll, no cost, automatic. You can still be deceived, but never puppeted, rewritten or read.
boons.flavour: Your mind is your own, and the door only opens from the inside. People who try to read you come away with nothing - no tells, no tics, no flicker behind the eyes to work with. People who try to push you find out that pushing was the only thing they brought.

boons.name: Jack of all Trades
boons.effect:
Bought as one of two tiers (the higher includes the lower's benefit - no need to buy both).
**Tier 1 (5, Greater)**: your baseline in every Skill is Trained, including ones you've never trained in or even heard named before - but your ceiling in any Skill is capped at Trained, permanently, even if you spend points to raise it further. Any of your 15-point Skills Pool left unspent because of that cap is simply unspent - it doesn't convert into points for Attributes, Resources, or anything else.
**Tier 2 (7, Legendary)**: the Tier 1 cap is lifted - Skills you specifically invest in can still climb past Trained toward Adept, Expert, or Master as normal.
boons.flavour: And a master of none. Being a jack of all trades is often better than mastery of a couple skills. You've picked up things here and there. None of it is remarkable, but you know how to do a little of everything and that matters more often.

boons.name: Lie Detector
boons.effect:
Bought as one of three tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one).
**Tier 1 (3, Lesser)**: for Insight rolls made specifically to catch someone in a lie, treat your [Skill Training Tier](skills.md#training-tiers) as one tier higher than your actual tier, with a minimum of Trained (same shape as [Double-Jointed](#boon-list)'s Escapology bump).
**Tier 2 (5, Greater)**: additionally, gain [Advantage](rules.md#advantage--disadvantage) on that same Insight roll, stacking with the Tier 1 bump - even a careful evasion or partial truth doesn't slip past easily.
**Tier 3 (7, Legendary)**: additionally, a direct, deliberate lie told straight to your face registers automatically, no roll needed - though you still won't know the truth, only that you weren't told it.
boons.flavour: It's never the words. Anyone can rehearse a story until it reads as true. It's the half-second hesitation, the glance away, the detail that is a little too on the nose. Everybody tells you when they are lying - you just know how to listen to what they are really saying.

boons.name: Light Sleeper
boons.effect:
Bought as one of three tiers (each includes the lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one).
**Tier 1 (1, Trivial)**: wake instantly at the slightest disturbance.
**Tier 2 (3, Lesser)**: additionally, you're never automatically [Surprised](rules.md#surprised) while asleep - roll Perception even while asleep to notice a threat, same as if you were awake.
**Tier 3 (5, Greater)**: additionally, waking from a disturbance doesn't cost you your position in the round - you act on your normal Initiative immediately rather than losing the first exchange getting your bearings.
boons.flavour: You have never slept through anything in your life. Most nights, it's a curse. You wake up before the sound is gone. You are awake and ready to go.

boons.name: Lightning Calculator
boons.effect: Instant, effortless mental processing of complex calculations - arithmetic, odds and statistics, trajectories, logistics, or any other math-driven estimate - done in your head, accurately, that would normally take pen, paper, or a calculator.
boons.flavour: You don't do the math. You don't have to - you just know the answer. The odds, how much fuel remains, the required angle to land the shot - the numbers are there. You are moving while everyone else is reaching for the calculator app on their phone.

boons.name: Natural Linguist
boons.effect:
Bought as one of four tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one).
**Tier 1 (1, Trivial)**: when first hearing an unfamiliar language, you can often piece together rough meaning and grammar patterns from listening alone (GM's call how much you catch).
**Tier 2 (3, Lesser)**: learn a new human language to fluency after a single day of real exposure or study.
**Tier 3 (5, Greater)**: learn a new human language to fluency after mere minutes of interaction.
**Tier 4 (7, Legendary)**: learn *any* language, including non-human or otherwise exotic communication systems - the time required scales with how alien it is (a terrestrial animal's calls might take a day; a species that communicates via color-shifting skin patches might take weeks).
boons.flavour: Some people have a knack for mathematics. Others have an ear for music. You have an innate understanding of languages. Within a few minutes of exposure to a language, you begin to understand it - where the verbs belong, which sounds are doing the heavy lifting, the patterns unique to the language. Give it a day, and you can survive.

boons.name: Never Off Balance
boons.effect: On a catastrophic failure on an attack roll, roll again. If the second roll succeeds, the catastrophic failure is downgraded to an ordinary miss - it never becomes a hit, and if the second roll also fails the catastrophic failure stands. The same shape as [Master](skills.md#training-tiers), for the one roll no Training Tier reaches.
boons.flavour: You've fallen (or been knocked down) enough times to have an opinion about it. You lose your footing and you are already recovering.

boons.name: Quick Study
boons.effect: Pick up new information or a demonstrated technique unusually fast, and read or skim at exceptional speed - GM's call on how much time it actually saves.
boons.flavour: One quick read through is usually all it takes. People don't like it when you pick something up over an afternoon that they spent the last five years mastering.

boons.name: Restful Trance
boons.effect: A Full Night's Rest only requires **3 hours** of actual sleep to grant its full benefit. A [Short Rest](rules.md#rests) only requires **15 minutes** instead of the normal hour, though the normal one-per-Full-Night's-Rest cap still applies.
boons.flavour: Three hours of meditation and you feel like a million bucks. You don't dream, toss and turn, or drift off to sleep - you turn your brain off and flip it back on just as easily. No one who sees it thinks it looks restful, but they don't know what they are missing.

boons.name: Special Movement
boons.effect: Choose a specific, narrow locomotion trick that shouldn't work but does: **Water-Walking** (cross any liquid surface as easily as solid ground), **Wall-Crawling** (climb any surface, including ceilings, as easily and securely as flat ground), **Tunneling** (dig through earth, sand, or similarly soft material at your normal Movement Rate), or **Untrackable** (leave no scent, footprint, or trail; mundane tracking, and most supernatural tracking, simply fails to find a path). May be bought more than once; each purchase must choose a different mode.
boons.flavour: You move in a way most people can't - crawling up a wall, walking over snow without a trace, swinging on grappling hooks. Whatever the method, physics filed an objection and no one listened.

boons.name: Special Weapons
boons.effect:
Access to a single named weapon system, chosen when you take this and defined with the GM - including which Element rolls it, if anything about it is rolled at all. Bought as one of three tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one).
The lists below are examples, not a menu to choose from. If the thing you want is not on them, that is rather the point of the Boon - bring it to the GM and settle between you what it does.
**Tier 1 (3, Lesser)**: unusual rather than restricted, and the only route to the Exotic (ranged) Category - no weapon Skill reaches it. A blowgun, a flare gun or a net launcher, all three already statted in [Equipment](weapons.md); a speargun or a dart pistol would sit here too.
**Tier 2 (5, Greater)**: hardware that exists and is illegal for you to be holding. A flamethrower, a shoulder-launched rocket, a mortar, a vehicle-mounted minigun, a riot water cannon.
**Tier 3 (7, Legendary)**: something that should not exist at all. A prototype railgun, a directed-energy rifle, a blade that remembers everyone it has killed, a rifle built for one specific target and inert against anybody else.
boons.flavour: You have one specific piece of hardware that nobody should be walking around with, and you know exactly how it works. Where it came from is your business. Whether the paperwork exists is nobody's business. It is yours, it is the only one you get, and it does something a normal weapon cannot.

boons.name: Steadfast Presence
boons.effect:
Bought as one of three tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one).
**Tier 1 (3, Lesser)**: immune to fear - any attempt to frighten or intimidate you automatically fails.
**Tier 2 (5, Greater)**: additionally, allies within your [Movement Rate](rules.md#movement--range) are inspired by your presence, gaining [Advantage](rules.md#advantage--disadvantage) on any roll made to resist fear or intimidation.
**Tier 3 (7, Legendary)**: additionally, allies within that same range share your full immunity to fear - any attempt to frighten or intimidate them automatically fails too.
boons.flavour: Fear doesn't seem to be able to get a grip on you. You don't hide it well - you just don't really get scared and people can tell. When things go wrong, everyone in the room turns to you. Your stoicism in the face of adversity steadies those around you.

boons.name: Trained by a Master
boons.effect:
Bought as one of four tiers (each includes every lower tier's benefit - no need to buy more than one). Each tier named below grants one additional Skill you can name (up to 4 total) *and* one additional use per session (up to 4 total). At the moment of failure, freely choose which named Skill the use applies to - uses aren't locked to a specific Skill in advance, and can all be spent on a single Skill in the same session if you want.
**Tier 1 (1, Trivial)**: 1 named Skill, 1 use per session.
**Tier 2 (3, Lesser)**: 2 named Skills, 2 uses per session.
**Tier 3 (5, Greater)**: 3 named Skills, 3 uses per session.
**Tier 4 (7, Legendary)**: 4 named Skills, 4 uses per session. A spent use treats a failure on the chosen Skill as a success instead.
boons.flavour: Somebody who was genuinely the best taught you, and they didn't waste time on the flashy parts. They taught you what to do when it goes wrong. Years later, at the moment it goes wrong, you hear their voice and your hands are already doing it.

boons.name: Unshakeable Alibi
boons.effect: Always have a plausible, verifiable-sounding cover story ready on short notice - GM's call on how far it holds up under real scrutiny.
boons.flavour: You always have a story - a time, a place, a reason and enough inane details that nobody wants to hear them. It's not a lie - you were really there.

boons.name: Unstoppable
boons.effect: Being reduced to 0 [Health Levels](rules.md#health-levels) doesn't render you unconscious - you keep going into negative Health Levels, down to the same −(Health Levels) death threshold everyone eventually hits, instead of blacking out at 0. While in that negative range: (1) you're extremely hurt but conscious - you can talk, move, and act at rest with no restriction; (2) any exertion - combat, strenuous effort, or moving quickly - costs **1 Ki** per instance.
boons.flavour: What should leave you unconscious and bleeding on the floor, simply doesn't. You can still die, you are just conscious for it.

boons.name: Weathered
boons.effect: Shrug off extreme heat, cold, thin air, and harsh weather that would meaningfully slow or endanger an ordinary person, and hold your breath far longer than an ordinary person can.
boons.flavour: You never understood why people are constantly worried about the weather. You simply don't make it an issue. Heat that melts the dog, cold that drives people inside, hurricane force winds - none of it stops you. The cold never bothered you, anyway

resources.name: Base
resources.scales: How developed, defended, or well-equipped the headquarters/safehouse is

levels.1: A dedicated, secure space of your own - a real hideout, workshop, or safehouse beyond an ordinary home; basic, but defensible
levels.2: A proper base with solid amenities and dependable security
levels.3: Well-equipped, with real security and specialized rooms
levels.4: Fortified and staffed, with serious defenses and advanced equipment
levels.5: A near-impenetrable, fully self-sufficient stronghold

resources.flavour: Somewhere that is yours. A door you control, a lock you picked out, and nobody's name on the lease that you didn't want there. It might be a room over a garage or a whole floor nobody else visits. Either way, you can shut the door and breathe.

resources.name: Black Market Access
resources.scales: How deep into illegal or off-the-books trade the connections reach

levels.1: A single fence or dealer for common contraband
levels.2: A working relationship with a local black-market network - weapons, drugs, stolen goods
levels.3: Real standing with a regional network, access to rarer or more dangerous goods
levels.4: Deep pull into a national or international smuggling network, most anything can be found for a price
levels.5: A name in the black market itself - you don't just buy from the network, you're a fixture in it, able to source almost anything that exists

resources.flavour: There is a version of every store that doesn't ask, doesn't record and doesn't remember you came in. A guy with a van. A back room behind a laundromat. A number you text one word to. You know where those are.

resources.name: Contacts
resources.scales: How large, capable, or well-placed the network is

levels.1: One reliable contact for small favors or info
levels.2: A handful of contacts spanning a couple of fields
levels.3: A broad network spanning most of a city
levels.4: An extensive network with regional reach, including a few influential names
levels.5: A vast network reaching into any relevant field or region, including powerful people

resources.flavour: You don't know the answer. You know four people, and one of them does. A cop who owes you. A nurse who works nights. Somebody's cousin at the airport. It isn't what you know - it's who picks up when you call.

resources.name: Corporate Backing
resources.scales: How much a legitimate business entity can move, fund, or cover

levels.1: A small business willing to carry you on the books, light cover and minor funding
levels.2: A real company with legitimate revenue, able to fund modest operations and provide solid cover
levels.3: A mid-size company with real assets, capable of funding serious operations and absorbing real scrutiny
levels.4: A major regional company, resources and cover to match, capable of weathering real investigation
levels.5: A multinational corporation's backing, effectively bottomless resources and cover strong enough to survive nearly anything

resources.flavour: Something enormous and entirely legal has decided you are useful. It moves slowly, it moves in writing, and once it moves it is very hard to stop. There is a budget code with your name on it and a lawyer who already knows who you are.

resources.name: Debts Owed
resources.scales: How much real leverage is owed, in favors people can't easily refuse

levels.1: One person who owes you a real, acknowledged favor
levels.2: A small handful of people who owe you, each for something genuinely significant
levels.3: A broader circle of real debts, enough to call in meaningful help when it matters
levels.4: Debts owed by people with real capability or standing of their own, favors that can move real weight
levels.5: A web of serious debts reaching people of real power, the kind of leverage that can bend outcomes that matter

resources.flavour: People owe you. Not favors, exactly - the other kind. The kind nobody gets out of by saying they're busy. You don't bring it up often. You have never needed to. They remember.

resources.name: Fame
resources.scales: How widely recognized the character is, and how strongly people react to it

levels.1: Known within a small local circle
levels.2: Recognized across a city or subculture
levels.3: Known regionally or nationally
levels.4: Broadly famous - recognized by strangers regularly
levels.5: World-renowned, a household name

resources.flavour: People know your face. The room changes when you walk into it, and not always in the direction you would like. Strangers are friendly, or they aren't, and either way they decided something about you before you opened your mouth.

resources.name: Followers
resources.scales: How many, how skilled, or how loyal the group is

levels.1: A single loyal follower or apprentice
levels.2: A small handful of modestly capable followers
levels.3: A coordinated, reasonably capable crew
levels.4: A sizable, well-organized group with real capability
levels.5: A substantial, highly capable and loyal organization

resources.flavour: You have people who will actually go when you say go. Not fans. Not friends who would think about it and get back to you. People who turn up with a van at four in the morning and ask what it's for later.

resources.name: Fringe Benefit
resources.scales: The reach/exclusivity of the license, membership, clearance, or legal right

levels.1: A basic hobbyist license/membership
levels.2: A recognized professional credential (licensed trade, press pass)
levels.3: Restricted-access clearance - into secured facilities, government-adjacent circles
levels.4: High-level clearance - classified access, executive-level standing
levels.5: Near-total access - opens virtually any door in its domain

resources.flavour: A card, a title, a laminated badge, a line on a form. Most people don't know that door is a door. You have the thing that opens it, and nobody at the desk is going to argue with you about it.

resources.name: Guild Standing
resources.scales: How much rank and pull the character holds within a specific trade or professional body

levels.1: A dues-paying member in reasonably good standing
levels.2: A recognized, respected member, able to call in modest favors
levels.3: A senior member with real influence over local guild decisions
levels.4: A leadership figure, influence reaching the guild's regional or national body
levels.5: A defining figure within the guild itself, decisions of real consequence run through you

resources.flavour: Inside one trade, your name means something specific. You don't have to be in the room for it to mean it. People who have never met you know where you rank and behave accordingly.

resources.name: Informant Network
resources.scales: How wide and reliable the web of low-level eyes and ears is

levels.1: A couple of regular tipsters in one neighborhood
levels.2: A working network across a city - cabbies, bartenders, doormen - who pass along what they see
levels.3: A broad network spanning a whole city's worth of ordinary people, reliable and reasonably fast
levels.4: A network with regional reach, fast enough to catch developing situations as they happen
levels.5: An extensive network reaching anywhere relevant, near-real-time awareness of anything worth knowing

resources.flavour: A lot of people see a lot of small things. Doormen, dishwashers, the guy running the newsstand, the kid who is always outside. Not one of them knows anything important. All of them tell you what they saw.

resources.name: Legal Counsel
resources.scales: How capable and well-connected the lawyer or legal team is

levels.1: A single competent lawyer, reliable for everyday trouble
levels.2: A small firm that can handle real charges and knows which favors to call in
levels.3: A firm with real courtroom pull and connections into the local justice system
levels.4: A firm capable of making serious charges quietly disappear, with reach into regional courts and agencies
levels.5: Legal firepower capable of making almost anything short of the worst crimes vanish, nationally

resources.flavour: Somebody whose entire job is standing between you and the consequences, and who is very good at it. They answer at two in the morning. They don't ask what you did. They ask what you said, and to whom.

resources.name: Media Contact
resources.scales: How much a story can be shaped, planted, or killed before it runs

levels.1: One sympathetic local journalist willing to hear you out
levels.2: A standing relationship with a local outlet - can get a story placed or softened
levels.3: Real pull with a regional news network - can plant, spike, or reframe a story reliably
levels.4: Influence reaching national media - a story dies or runs the way you want it to, most of the time
levels.5: Command of the narrative at a national or international level - what the world believes happened is substantially up to you

resources.flavour: A story runs, or it doesn't. Somebody decides which, and you know them well enough to call. What ends up in the paper is not the same thing as what happened, and you have a hand in the difference.

resources.name: Medical Access
resources.scales: How much discreet, high-quality medical care can be called on

levels.1: A single sympathetic nurse or paramedic willing to patch you up off the books
levels.2: A private doctor who treats you (and a few others) no questions asked
levels.3: A small discreet clinic with real equipment, staffed by people who won't talk
levels.4: A private hospital wing or trauma team on standby, capable of handling serious, unusual injuries
levels.5: A world-class covert medical operation, capable of handling anything short of death itself, anywhere you can reach it

resources.flavour: Care that happens quietly and competently, with nobody filling out the form asking how this occurred. A clinic that keeps odd hours. A surgeon who owes somebody. You get stitched up and you go home.

resources.name: Occult Library
resources.scales: How comprehensive, rare, or dangerous the collection of esoteric material is

levels.1: A modest personal collection - well-thumbed books on folklore and the occult, covering common knowledge
levels.2: A solid working library, with enough breadth to research most common supernatural phenomena and a few genuine rarities
levels.3: An extensive collection, including forbidden or suppressed texts - enough to dig into obscure or actively dangerous topics
levels.4: A renowned archive sought after by scholars and occultists alike, holding material found nowhere else publicly
levels.5: A legendary collection - texts thought lost or mythical; knowledge dangerous enough that possessing it alone draws attention

resources.flavour: Shelves of things most people would find unbearably dull and a few people would burn the building down to reach. Some of it is photocopied. Some of it should never have been photocopied. You know where every piece of it is.

resources.name: Safehouse Network
resources.scales: How many scattered bolt-holes are maintained, and how well hidden each is

levels.1: One bolt-hole beyond your Base. Somewhere to lie up for a night that nothing on paper connects to you
levels.2: A small handful across a city, none of them connected to each other or to you
levels.3: A network spanning a region, each site far enough off the road that nobody arrives by accident
levels.4: A network reaching into neighboring regions, a few of them hidden well enough to survive a real search
levels.5: A network at national scale, any site of which can disappear you completely, indefinitely

resources.flavour: Somewhere to go that isn't home, in more than one direction, already stocked. Cash, a change of clothes, a phone nobody has the number for. You have never needed all of them at once. You keep them all anyway.

resources.name: Sanctuary Standing
resources.scales: How protected the character is within one specific safe territory

levels.1: A single establishment where you're recognized and safe from casual trouble
levels.2: A small protected zone - a block, a building complex - where real trouble is unwelcome
levels.3: A genuine sanctuary territory, actively enforced, real consequences for violating it
levels.4: A significant, well-known sanctuary, respected and enforced across multiple factions
levels.5: A sanctuary recognized and honored practically everywhere relevant, violating it carries consequences almost no one is willing to risk

resources.flavour: There is one patch of ground where nothing touches you, and everybody standing on it knows why. Get through that door and whatever is chasing you has to stop and think it over.

resources.name: Signature Possession
resources.scales: How significant the one prized item owned actually is

levels.1: A well-made, quality item - reliable, a cut above ordinary
levels.2: An item with a real history or reputation of its own, recognized by those who know to look
levels.3: A genuinely rare or exceptional item, sought after by serious collectors or rivals
levels.4: An item of real renown, recognized on sight by anyone versed in its field
levels.5: A legendary item, known even to people who've never seen it - and often coveted because of it

resources.flavour: One object. Yours specifically, known to be yours, and worth something to somebody other than you. A car, a watch, an instrument, a gun with a history. People recognize it before they recognize you.

resources.name: Spiritual Standing
resources.scales: How much weight the character's name carries within a specific religious or spiritual community

levels.1: A respected member of a local congregation or circle
levels.2: A trusted figure within a wider spiritual community, sought out for guidance
levels.3: Real authority within the community - your word carries weight in real decisions
levels.4: A recognized leader or elder, influence reaching related communities elsewhere
levels.5: A figure of real spiritual significance, recognized and deferred to across the faith or tradition broadly

resources.flavour: Within one faith, your word carries weight that has nothing to do with what you can prove. People listen because of where you stand, not because of the argument you made. That cuts both ways and you know it.

resources.name: System Access
resources.scales: How deep and wide the character's reach into digital systems and networks already is

levels.1: Access to public records and consumer-level databases and systems
levels.2: Real internal access into a specific organization's systems - a company, a local agency
levels.3: Broad access spanning multiple systems and networks, reaching into mid-level corporate or government databases
levels.4: Deep access into high-security systems - classified government or corporate networks, real backdoors
levels.5: Near-total digital reach - access into almost any system that exists, the kind of reach that alarms anyone who learns of it

resources.flavour: Doors that aren't doors, opened with credentials that are genuinely yours. You aren't breaking in. You are logging in, and the log says you were supposed to be there.

resources.name: Territory
resources.scales: How much real ground answers to the character specifically

levels.1: A single block or building genuinely under your influence
levels.2: A modest neighborhood where your word carries real weight
levels.3: A significant district, actively held and defended
levels.4: A substantial stretch of a city, real infrastructure and people answering to you
levels.5: Territory on the scale of a city or region, genuinely yours in every practical sense

resources.flavour: Actual ground that answers to you. Not owned - owned is a different thing, and much easier. Nobody deals on this block, drinks in this bar or parks on this street without it getting back to you.

resources.name: Underworld Reputation
resources.scales: How known, trusted, or feared the character is within criminal and hidden-world circles

levels.1: A name a few low-level players recognize and treat with mild caution
levels.2: Known within a specific city's criminal scene as someone not worth crossing
levels.3: Respected or feared across a city's underworld broadly, name carries real weight in negotiations
levels.4: Known regionally among serious players - crime bosses, cartels, syndicates - as someone to reckon with
levels.5: A legend in the underworld nationally or beyond, invoked as a cautionary tale or a name that opens (or closes) any door

resources.flavour: In the parts of town with no signage, people have heard of you, and they have heard something specific. You never have to introduce yourself. You do occasionally have to correct the story.

resources.name: Vehicle
resources.scales: How distinctive, capable, or valuable the vehicle is

levels.1: Reliable but unremarkable
levels.2: One standout feature - notably fast, armored, or distinctive
levels.3: Significantly customized, high-performance
levels.4: Rare and exceptional - armored, military-grade, or famous
levels.5: One-of-a-kind, legendary in capability or reputation

resources.flavour: It gets you there, and people notice which one it is. That's the trade. Everybody remembers the car, which is wonderful right up until somebody is describing it to a police sketch artist.

resources.name: Wealth
resources.scales: How much disposable financial resource is available to draw on

levels.1: Financially comfortable - bills, rent, and daily needs covered without stress, plus modest savings and room for the occasional splurge
levels.2: Well-off - real disposable income, enough saved to absorb an emergency without real strain
levels.3: Wealthy; owns property outright, can make major purchases freely
levels.4: Very wealthy; can finance a major undertaking outright
levels.5: A fortune large enough to move markets or bankroll entire operations

resources.flavour: Money you can actually reach, which is a different thing from money you technically have. Net worth is a number on paper. This is what's in the account on a Tuesday, and it's the only one that matters when you need something today.

gifts.markdown:
### Alternate Form

Your body was the first draft. You decided to design a second one. Bones slide over one another. Muscle and skin ripple with a mind of their own. Shifting between the two takes a moment. The first time was awful - itchy, painful... and the sound. Now, you can do it while holding a conversation.

Transforming is a Slow action and triggers a [Gift Check](#resolution) - success free, failure costs 1 Ki, the transformation happens either way. The form lasts until voluntarily dropped, no ongoing cost to maintain.

The alternate form is built once, at creation, spending a points pool (below) on the build menu below. The pool scales with Gift Level, so a character can revisit and add to the form's build as they gain Levels.

**Pool by Level**:

| Level | Pool |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 points |
| 2 | 5 points |
| 3 | 9 points |
| 4 | 13 points |
| 5 | 18 points |

**Build menu**:

| Option | Cost | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Sub-stat boost | 1 pt | +2 to one physical sub-stat (Soak, Ferocity, Stamina, Potence, or Initiative) while transformed. |
| Attribute boost | 2 pts/point | +1 to one Attribute (Earth, Air, Fire, Water, or Moira) while transformed, up to your own normal maximum. |
| Environmental adaptation | 1 pt | Breathe underwater, see in total darkness, ignore extreme temperatures, or similar. |
| Borrow a Gift Level | 3 pts/Level | Gain one Level of an existing Gift you don't otherwise hold while transformed, GM-approved for fit - same per-Level price as the [Gifts pool](character-creation.md#10-gifts). |
| Borrow a Boon | 1/3/5/7 pts | Gain a Boon you don't otherwise hold while transformed, at that Boon's own Trivial/Lesser/Greater/Legendary price. |

**Adders**:

- **Partial Shift** (Lesser, 3 pts): shift a single body part (hands to claws, eyes, wings) without a full transformation - no action cost, no Gift Check - but only one build-menu option's benefit applies at a time, not the whole form.
- **Extended Reserve** (Greater, 6 pts): the build-menu pool at every Level is permanently +3 points bigger.
- **Second Form** (Greater, 6 pts): build a second alternate form at creation, chosen independently, with its own full pool for your Level. Switching still triggers the Gift Check each time.
- **Snap Change** (Lesser, 3 pts): transforming is a Fast action instead of a Slow one. The Gift Check still applies.
- **Shed Skin** (Greater, 6 pts): once per Scene, when a hit would cost you a Health Level while transformed, you drop back to your normal form instead and ignore that Health Level. You can't transform again until the Scene ends.
- **Terrifying Visage** (Lesser, 3 pts): the first time per Scene you transform in sight of enemies, roll your Level plus half your Presence against the Presence of every enemy within Close; a connecting die leaves that enemy Frightened until the end of their next turn.
- **Final Stage** (Greater, 6 pts): once per Scene while transformed, spend 2 Ki: every sub-stat boost in your build counts twice until the Scene ends. When the Scene ends you revert and are Exhausted until your next Short Rest.
- **Mending Shift** (Lesser, 3 pts): transforming or reverting ends any Bleeding or Envenomed condition on you, as the body rebuilds itself.

**Limiters**:

- **Slow to Invoke**: transforming takes a full Minute instead of a Slow action.
- **Involuntary Trigger**: the form activates automatically under a specific stress condition (mortal danger, strong emotion, GM's call at creation) and can't be suppressed once triggered.
- **Fixed Duration**: the form can't be voluntarily dropped early. It lasts a flat Scene, then reverts on its own.
- **Painful Change**: every transformation, in or out, leaves you Staggered until the end of your next turn.
- **Beast Mind**: while transformed you can't speak, and you're at Disadvantage on every Mental roll.
- **Keyed Trigger**: you can only transform while holding one specific item chosen at creation (a mask, a charm, a card). Lose it and you can't transform until it's back in your hand.
- **Carried Weakness**: choose one weakness at creation (fire, silver, cold iron, loud noise). While transformed, attacks that use it against you roll at Advantage.

gifts.name: Animal Friendship

adders.name: Beast Steed
adders.text: your Animal Companion can carry you as a mount. While mounted, your Movement Rate matches the Companion's own.

adders.name: Speak for the Wild

adders.text: your attacks against a target your Animal Companion is in Melee with are at Advantage. Can't be taken with **No Companion**.

adders.text: once per Scene, when a hit would land on you, your Animal Companion within Close throws itself in the way and takes the hit instead. Can't be taken with **No Companion**.

adders.name: Beast Fusion
adders.text: once per Scene, spend 2 Ki as a Slow action to merge with your Animal Companion until the Scene ends: you gain all its sub-stat bonuses from Levels 3-5 on top of your own, and it can't act separately. Requires Level 3. Can't be taken with **No Companion**.

adders.name: Call of the Wild
adders.text: once per Scene, spend 2 Ki: every animal within a long walk hears you and arrives within a few rounds, a group you can direct as at Level 3, even where none were in sight. Requires Level 3.

limiters.name: Single Species
limiters.text: the Gift only works on one chosen species, not animals in general.

limiters.name: No Companion
limiters.text: you never gain the free Animal Companion at Level 2. Like every Limiter, this is permanent - it defines what the Gift is, and no amount of XP removes it. Can't be taken with **Beast Steed**, **Swarm Companion** or **Second Companion**.

limiters.text: using the Gift requires speaking or making an audible animal call. Doesn't work if you're silenced, gagged, or otherwise unable to vocalize.

limiters.name: Shared Wounds
limiters.text: whenever your Animal Companion loses a Health Level, you lose 1 Poise and are Distracted until the end of your next turn. Can't be taken with **No Companion**.

limiters.text: every task you direct an animal to do (Level 2+) must be paid for with food or a comfort it wants. Unpaid, your next roll with any animal is at Disadvantage until you settle it.

limiters.text: you carry the wild on you: Disadvantage on Social rolls with people while your Animal Companion or any animal you're directing is in sight.

levels.effect: Roll **Moira + Difficulty** to calm an agitated animal or exchange simple, instinct-level understanding with it (hunger, fear, the direction of danger) - one ordinary animal at a time, within Close range. Is a Normal action. No Ki, no Gift Check.

Range extends to **Near**. You may now direct the animal to perform one simple task within its natural capabilities (lead you somewhere, retrieve a small object, stand guard, fetch help) in addition to calming or understanding it. Still a Normal action, no Ki. Additionally, you gain a lasting **Animal Companion**, free with this Level - no Ki or point cost - an ordinary creature of your choice, chosen at creation, that stays by your side simply because it likes you. Not summoned or magically bound; it can leave if truly mistreated or endangered, but under normal circumstances it travels and fights alongside you.

Range extends to **Far**. You may now affect a small group of animals simultaneously (a pack, a flock, a swarm) rather than just one - calming, understanding, or directing all of them at once costs **1 Ki**. Your Animal Companion's bond deepens automatically, free with this Level: it gains **+2** to one relevant sub-stat of your choice (Soak, Ferocity, Stamina, Potence, or Initiative).

The affected group scales up to a full herd, swarm, or pack of any size. Your influence now extends to dangerous or exotic wildlife, not just ordinary animals - even apex predators respond to you. Group-effect Ki cost rises to **2**. Your Animal Companion gains a second **+2** to a different sub-stat, automatically, free with this Level (stacking with Level 3's bonus).

Your connection extends even to legendary or mythic beasts - dragons, cryptids, spirits wearing animal shape, whatever the setting allows (GM's call on fit). Group-effect Ki cost drops back to **1**. Your Animal Companion gains a third **+2** to a sub-stat of your choice, plus one minor Boon-equivalent trait fitting the bond (GM-approved) - both automatic, free with this Level.

adders.name: Cold Read

adders.name: Second Read

limiters.name: Human Tells
limiters.text: reads only work on creatures with a human-like body. Animals, machines, the dead, swarms and anything without breath or a face can't be read.

### Battle Sense

Everyone telegraphs every move. Most people just don't know Morse code. You are able to read the subtle tells that reveal what your opponent will do - a sharp intake of breath, a subtle shift in stance, an involuntary glance where they will strike. It's not precognition and it's no use outside of a fight, but you see it coming before they know they are going to do it.

Reading an opponent costs **1 Ki**, declared on your turn - it takes no action. You can hold **one read at a time**; naming somebody new drops the one you had.

adders.name: Onboard AI

adders.name: Hidden Arsenal

adders.name: Cortex Vault
adders.text: Your brain lives in an armored case. When you would die, your body is wrecked but you survive in the case - helpless, but able to hear, speak through a Comms Array, and be installed in a new body after a week of downtime. The Vault can't save you again until that week is done.

limiters.name: Visible Hardware
